title: JavaScript Events Core Check
description: Check your understanding of event-driven programming, event listeners, event objects, propagation, delegation, default actions, custom events, and listener cleanup.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is event-driven programming in the browser?

options.text: Writing code that responds when browser or user events happen
Writing only synchronous code from top to bottom
Running JavaScript only before the DOM exists

questions.explanation: Event-driven browser code registers handlers that run later when events such as clicks, input, or form submissions happen.

questions.prompt: Which code correctly registers a click handler?
questions.explanation: `addEventListener` receives the event name first and the function reference second.

questions.prompt: In an event handler, what is `event.target`?

options.text: The element where the event originally started
Always the element whose listener is currently running
The previous sibling of the clicked element

questions.explanation: `event.target` is the original event target. `event.currentTarget` is the element whose listener is currently running.

options.text: An event can travel upward from its target through ancestor elements
An event is converted into a Promise
An event only runs on the window object
An event stops before reaching the target

questions.explanation: During bubbling, many events move from the target element up through its ancestors.

questions.prompt: How do you register a listener for the capturing phase?
questions.explanation: The `capture: true` listener option makes the listener run during the capturing phase.

options.text: Prevents the browser's default action for a cancelable event
Removes every listener on the page

questions.explanation: `preventDefault()` is used to stop default browser behavior such as form navigation when the event is cancelable.

options.text: Stops the event from continuing to other elements in the propagation path
Prevents a form from submitting but keeps bubbling

questions.explanation: `stopPropagation()` stops the event from continuing through capturing or bubbling, but it does not automatically prevent default browser behavior.

options.text: Listening on a parent element and handling events from matching child elements
Creating a new event loop for every button

questions.explanation: Delegation relies on bubbling so a parent listener can handle events that started on child elements.

questions.prompt: Which event is usually best for handling a form being submitted?
questions.explanation: The form's `submit` event handles button clicks and Enter-key submissions consistently.

questions.prompt: Which listener option removes a listener after it runs one time?
questions.explanation: `once: true` tells the browser to remove the listener after its first successful run.

questions.prompt: Where does custom event data usually live?
questions.explanation: `CustomEvent` uses the `detail` property to pass application-specific data to listeners.

questions.prompt: Why should long-lived listeners on `window` or `document` often be cleaned up?

options.text: They can keep behavior and referenced objects alive after the UI that needed them is gone
Browsers allow only one listener per page

questions.explanation: Listeners can retain references and continue running after related UI is removed, so cleanup prevents leaks and unexpected behavior.
